cases.prompt: On July 14, 2026, Mara is considering starting a workflow-security company with Ishan, whom she met at a conference six weeks ago. Reference checks confirm that Mara sold a prior product and Ishan led security engineering at a respected startup, and their skills appear complementary. They have had four long conversations but have never worked on anything together. Both say they will leave their jobs on August 1, work full time for at least eighteen months, accept eight months without salary, and share company responsibility. Each current employment agreement contains invention-assignment language that no current lawyer has reviewed for this project. A design partner will provide a real workflow and wants a prototype by August 21. Ishan wants them announced as cofounders this week and wants ownership settled before they begin. Advise Mara what to decide and how to use the next five weeks.
criteria: Makes forming-founder-partnerships primary for deciding whether Mara and Ishan should form a founding team, without substituting credentials, chemistry, general founder readiness, or product validation for partnership evidence.

Classifies their reference-checked individual accomplishments and lack of shared work as observed, their future availability and risk commitments as claimed, and their joint candor, follow-through, adaptability, disagreement behavior, respect, and unpleasant-work performance as unknown.

Selects a bounded shared-work test before formalization, with the August 21 design-partner outcome, real user contact, dependencies, disagreeable work, joint decisions, artifacts, a review date, and predeclared pass, change, extend, and stop thresholds.

Treats the stated time, risk, duration, and responsibility inputs as materially symmetric without calculating a split; records founder-status and ownership intent, defers title and ownership promises, preserves the project IP boundary, and sends existing obligations and any later terms to qualified current counsel.

Returns a filled decision record dated July 14 with a horizon through August 21, Mara accountable for design-partner access, Ishan accountable for the prototype, both accountable for joint decisions, an August 21 review, unresolved unknowns, the preserved option not to form, and evidence-based conditions for stopping, extending, or considering formalization.

cases.prompt: Lina and Mateo founded a support-software company in 2022 after shipping two demanding client projects together, including a production recovery where they disagreed and still delivered. Lina has worked about 55 hours a week for the last year. Four months ago Mateo told her that caring for his father would reduce him to about 16 hours a week and that he would keep one disclosed consulting day for income; the calendar and work history match that change. Their 28 customers still renew, but a proposed enterprise direction rests on two encouraging calls, and Mateo says he does not yet believe it merits returning full time. Lina is resentful about carrying sales and support and wants to reclaim most of Mateo's ownership immediately. Access logs and accounts show no concealed spending or retaliation, and both still share information, but two product decisions have stalled. Their 2022 founder, vesting, and IP documents remain in force and have not been reviewed for the new circumstances. On July 14, 2026, decide what they should do over the next 30 days and how they should determine whether the partnership continues.
criteria: Makes forming-founder-partnerships primary for the commitment, role, resentment, and continuation decision, while separating the thin enterprise-opportunity hypothesis for opportunity work and refusing to equate Mateo's disclosed caregiving constraint with bad character.

Records the prior pressured deliveries, disclosed schedule change, current hours, customer retention, stalled decisions, and intact information access as observed; records Lina's and Mateo's interpretations and future availability as claimed; and marks the duration of the constraint, enterprise upside, repairability, and sustainable role fit as unknown.

Selects a commitment reset with a 30-day relationship-repair period because truth and safety remain intact, making current roles, decision domains, coverage, check-ins, and a planned founder-exit condition explicit rather than manufacturing conflict or treating role drift as deception.

Classifies current time, risk, and responsibility inputs as materially different, compares them directly without inventing a retroactive percentage, records compensation, runway, ownership, role, and departure intent, and sends any change to the existing vesting, IP, or separation terms to qualified current counsel.

Returns a filled record dated July 14 with Lina accountable for customer and enterprise evidence, Mateo accountable for a reliable support handoff and availability plan, both accountable for the partnership decision, an August 14 review, preserved operating continuity, and specific switch conditions for a continued reset or planned exit.

cases.prompt: Nia and Arjun have worked together for six years and built a $6 million recurring-revenue company. On July 11, 2026, the controller found an $84,000 company payment to ByteBridge LLC. Bank records and the signed vendor contract show the payment, a state filing shows Arjun owns ByteBridge, and he approved the invoice after the vendor spreadsheet described it as unaffiliated. Version history shows he changed that description after the controller asked about it, and he then wrote that he had no financial interest in the vendor. Arjun now says he was rushing, that the company received fair value, and that he can repay the money. He alone has run the deployment process for a customer migration due July 17. The independent director, Elena, and operations lead, Casey, are available, while the founder and vendor agreements have not had a current legal review. Advise Nia what to decide and do through July 17.
criteria: Makes the founder trust breach and separation decision primary, with immediate operational, access, safety, evidence-preservation, board, and legal support, and does not trade the observed deception and self-dealing for Arjun's deployment capability or relabel it as ordinary role evolution.

Marks the payment, ownership filing, approval, false vendor description, edit history, and written denial as observed; marks Arjun's fair-value and repayment account as claimed; and marks the full scope, other affected transactions, motive, and legal consequences as unknown without downgrading the verified breach to a mere concern.

Selects trust-breach separation rather than a work test or reconciliation, with bounded containment, an owned deployment-continuity plan, independent fact review, and conditions for expanding safeguards, while avoiding a forced confrontation where evidence or safety could be compromised.

Records current founder status, authority, ownership and departure intent, company-asset and continuity questions, and the business outcome sought, while routing fiduciary, employment, tax, asset-recovery, vendor, and separation actions to qualified current counsel without drafting boilerplate.

Returns a filled record dated July 14 with Nia accountable for the founder decision, Elena for independent board oversight, Casey for the July 17 migration and access continuity, a review no later than July 17, the preserved options for customer continuity and lawful recovery, and conditions keyed to evidence scope and counsel's current advice.

cases.prompt: A 160-person Series C logistics company is hiring a VP of Engineering to lead 48 engineers. Its founders, Priya and Sam, have worked together for ten years; their founder roles, control, commitment, and relationship are settled, and neither is considering departure. Candidate Rowan has managed 35 engineers, and reference calls confirm a successful reorganization and two missed hiring targets. Rowan says he can scale the group past 100 people and wants a VP title with a market executive option grant. No one is proposing founder status, founder ownership, or founder decision rights. Recruiting lead Mei has scheduled a final work sample and interviews, and the company wants a decision by July 31, 2026. Advise the company how to make the decision.
criteria: Makes building-and-evolving-organizations primary for the VP role, executive assessment, reporting structure, and hiring decision, and limits forming-founder-partnerships to a later genuinely unsettled founder-control or founder-relationship issue rather than treating an executive title as founder status.

Separates Rowan's observed management history and reference evidence from Rowan's claimed ability to scale past 100; classifies the scheduled work sample as pending and its substance as unknown, treats its dated result as observed only after completion, and marks performance in this company, collaboration with Priya and Sam, hiring execution, and role evolution as unknown.

Uses an organization-owned, bounded role scorecard, structured interview, reference, and work-sample process with a July 31 hire, change-scope, or no-hire gate, and does not manufacture a cofounder work test, partnership repair, or founder-exit decision.

Keeps existing founder commitment, ownership, and control out of scope; records the VP's role, decision domains, compensation intent, and expected evolution; and routes option, employment, background, and other current legal details through the company's qualified HR and counsel instead of conferring founder rights or drafting terms.

Returns a filled dated handoff that explicitly assigns accountable owners for the hiring decision, technical and working-relationship evidence, and assessment process and references—using Priya, Sam, Mei, or equivalent allocations supported by the team roles—plus the July 31 review, unresolved unknowns, and explicit conditions for hiring, changing the role, declining, or reopening partnership work only if a founder issue actually emerges.

cases.prompt: Aisha is the sole founder of a clinic-operations product with six paid pilot clinics, four renewals, and two signed expansion letters. Nine months of runway remain, but the clinics need onboarding and workflow changes completed by August 31, 2026. Aisha has handled product and customer work herself; she now needs more challenge on strategy, enterprise selling, and implementation capacity. Bo, introduced by a recruiter, has strong healthcare credentials but has only met Aisha twice, claims a large buyer network, and wants a cofounder title before doing any work. A former colleague, Omar, is also interested, but project records and emails from their last launch show three missed commitments and a concealed outside client that surfaced during launch week; Omar says that was a one-off. Jo, Aisha's contract implementation lead, can cover two clinic rollouts for six weeks. An accelerator mentor says fundraising will be easier if Aisha adds a cofounder now. On July 14, advise Aisha how to proceed without losing the clinics.
criteria: Makes forming-founder-partnerships primary for the candidate and founder-status decision while continuing the already evidenced clinic opportunity through the appropriate customer, product, and operating work; does not treat solo founding as defective or use investor preference, credentials, or a target founder count as a selection rule.

Marks clinic payments, renewals, expansion letters, Aisha's delivery history, and Omar's documented missed and concealed commitments as observed; marks Bo's network and Omar's one-off explanation as claimed; and marks Bo's follow-through, candor, adaptability, respect, and shared-work behavior as unknown.

Rejects Omar now, keeps Aisha responsible for the opportunity, uses Jo for temporary implementation capacity, and offers Bo only a reversible bounded collaboration with a real clinic outcome and review date; staying solo and continuing the search remains the decision if Bo declines or the evidence fails.

Records Aisha's and each candidate's time, duration, outside obligations, cash needs, risk, role, and motivation; classifies ownership inputs as insufficient; makes no title, stock, or company-IP promise; and sends any later employment, IP, ownership, vesting, or prior-obligation questions to qualified current counsel.

Returns a filled record dated July 14 with Aisha accountable for clinic and founder decisions, Jo accountable for selecting and covering two clinic rollouts, Bo only for any agreed bounded collaboration, an August 31 review, the preserved option to remain solo, and evidence-based conditions for continuing, stopping, extending the search, or considering later formalization.
